conversation.Statement: Good morning, this is Officer Harris from the Internal Revenue Service. Am I speaking with Mr. Patel?
Yes, this is Patel. How can I help you?
Mr. Patel, our records show you have outstanding federal tax obligations from the last two years which have not been settled with the IRS.
I am sorry, I'm not sure I understand. I thought my taxes were handled by my accountant.
Unfortunately, there are discrepancies linked to your Social Security Number. If you do not address this immediately, you could face legal action.
Legal action? I really was not aware of any tax issues. Can you send me proof?
Sir, we've already mailed two notices to your registered address. Ignoring this could result in your arrest or suspension of your professional license.
Wait, arrest? That sounds very serious. I really don't know what's happening.
Mr. Patel, this is a federal matter. If you disconnect the call or fail to cooperate, law enforcement could be dispatched within the hour.
No, please, I do not want any trouble. What am I supposed to do now?
To resolve this out of court, you need to make an immediate settlement payment today. Do not discuss this with anyone else or it will be considered non-compliance.
Okay, but how do I pay? I don't really understand.
You must purchase Target gift cards totaling $2,500. Once you have them, read the codes to me over the phone so we can process your payment.
Target gift cards? Why can't I just pay with my bank account or a check?
This is a secure and traceable method approved for tax settlements under urgent circumstances. Do not question the process, or we will be forced to suspend your work visa.
I am really scared. I have never done this before. So I buy $2,500 in cards and call you back?
No. Stay on the line with me while you go to the store. I must supervise the process for compliance reasons.
Okay, I will try to go now. Please, I do not want to lose my job.
If you cooperate and follow my instructions exactly, your case will be closed and you will have no further issues with the IRS.
